summary: Gadsden County fire tower named on a Chattahoochee map; the only dated event is a 2005 bid sale, and no source gives a build date or present condition.

events.note: Bids opened for the sale of the tower; winning bid $1,011. The directory does not name the buyer or say where the tower went.

evidence.supports: Rosedale record lists the tower in Gadsden County
Map listing names a Rosedale Fire Tower among its places
The map page lists named places for the Chattahoochee area
Bids for the sale of the tower opened 14 September 2005; winning bid $1,011
evidence.quote: September 14, 2005: Bids were opened for the sale of the tower, winning bid was for $1011.00.

evidence.supports: Florida Forest Service fire towers no longer needed are sold as surplus state property
evidence.quote: those items are sold as surplus state property

evidence.supports: The high bidder is expected to dismantle and deliver a surplus fire tower
evidence.quote: The high bidder is expected to dismantle and deliver the tower to its new destination.

sources.title: Surplus Equipment and Fire Towers
sources.publisher: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services

notes_for_editor: Only three sources touch this tower, and none gives a build date, height, design, agency or present condition. The directory gives Gadsden County and the 2005 bid sale. The map listing confirms the name Rosedale Fire Tower in the Chattahoochee area. The directory does not tie its 2005 sale record to a name beyond Rosedale, so linking that sale to this tower is an inference the editor should weigh. The surplus page describes the general Florida Forest Service process and does not mention Rosedale. The tower is not in the NHLR or FFLOS Florida lists in the local cache. Possible checks: Florida Forest Service surplus records for 2005, and Gadsden County or Tallahassee newspapers from September 2005. Record coordinates (30.65688, -84.82123) were not checked against a map.
